title: Those evening bells
html_source: “Those Evening Bells” is the title of another Thomas Moore song. The lyrics add to the melancholy of this part of the chapter, and of a sense of nostalgia and lost youthful innocence that seem to affect Bloom. “Those evening bells! those evening bells! / How many a tale their music tells, / Of youth and home, and that sweet time, / When I last heard their soothing chime…. / And so ‘twill be when I am gone, / That tuneful peal will still ring on, / While other bards shall walk these dells, / And sing your praise, sweet evening bells.” Since Joyce seems to have also obsessed over competition from “other bards” than himself who then, and would later, walk the dells of Ireland.
